articleTitle: Matching network absorption in ladder electroacoustic filters
abstract: This paper explores a synthesis approach to integrate the lumped elements of the input and output matching networks within the electroacoustic filter structure itself directly during the synthesis process. This integration allows for the removal of external matching components while preserving the necessary impedance matching conditions at both the input and output interfaces, thereby improving the efficiency and practicality of filter network designs.

articleTitle: Filtering Microstrip to Waveguide Launcher
abstract: This paper presents a novel synthesis-based co-design of a filtering microstrip-to-waveguide launcher. The proposed design is intended to replace the waveguide low-pass filter generally placed between the common port of the diplexer and the antenna port in FDD communication systems. The launcher is truly considered part of the filter since it acts as the last resonator of its prototype model. The overall frequency behavior is then completed with microstrip stubs (extracted-poles) connected through suitable transmission lines. A methodological design procedure is presented for this purpose together with a practical implementation centered in the X-band (8 – 12 GHz). Full-wave simulations and measurements are in agreement and they validate the proposed design with clear advantages in terms of out-of-band performance and reduced system complexity.

articleTitle: Direct Band-Pass Synthesis of Wideband Reactive Filter based on Matrix Rotations
abstract: A synthesis method of wideband filter based on reactive components is presented using the Coupling Matrix (CM) through direct bandpass synthesis. Leveraged in the classical nodal representation of the CM, different topologies can be explored by applying matrix operations such as inversion, similarity transformations and partitioning. In order to easily understand the couplings interactions in a topology, it is convenient to associate these lumped elements with their nodal representation. Applying the proposed synthesis method, all the values of the lumped elements can be successfully extracted without any optimization in the prototype model. Then, the obtained values are scaled in frequency and subsequently adjusted to be able to manufacture the filter. In this scenario, a third-order bandpass filter with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) around 40 % and two transmission zeros (TZ) in the upper band are synthesized in order to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Lowpass-Bandpass Filter with Three Element Resonator Configuration
abstract: This paper presents a new type of the lumped element dual-band lowpass-bandpass filter network and its numerical synthesis method based on the objective function. Two synthesized examples with the different passband widths illustrate the effectiveness of the synthesis method. As a prototype circuit it provides a good candidate for the design of the dual-band lowpass-bandpass filter up to microwave frequency band since it can be easily transformed into a distributed circuit of physically realizable configuration. The measured results of the fabricated filter up to 2700MHz validates experimentally the prototype filter.

articleTitle: Novel Negative Coupling Structure for Rectangular Waveguide Cavity Filters
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel negative coupling structure that is suitable for fabrication using milling and micromachining technologies. The proposed negative coupling structure is designed in three sections: a central bow-shaped iris is sandwiched between two sections that manipulate electro-magnetic fields, causing a 180-degree phase rotation. To validate this concept, we have developed a silicon micromachined fourth-degree quasi-elliptic bandpass filter with a center frequency of 270 GHz and a fractional bandwidth of 2.2%. The measured results of the filter display two transmission zeros in the stopband thus demonstrating the correct performance of the negative coupling structure.

Author Keywords: millimeter wave and terahertz components and technologies

articleTitle: Ku-band MUX Based On Ceramic-loaded Barrel-shaped For High-power Satellite Applications
abstract: In this paper the first experimental results of a compact multiplexer for satellite high-power applications at Ku-band are shown. The multiplexer is based on ceramic-loaded combline resonators with a customized-shape. The geometries and the materials have been chosen in order to improve the performance in terms of power-handling and multipactor up to 75–150W continuous wave of the input RF power. Barrel-shaped metal cavities are combined with ceramic materials in order to minimize the volume occupation maintaining high unloaded Q-factor values (>4000). The CAD results of the high-power and environmental analyses are presented.

articleTitle: 38.7 GHz Thin Film Lithium Niobate Acoustic Filter
abstract: In this work, a 38.7 GHz acoustic wave ladder filter exhibiting insertion loss (IL) of 5.63 dB and 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 17.6% is demonstrated, pushing the frequency limits of thin-film piezoelectric acoustic filter technology. The filter achieves operating frequency up to 5G millimeter wave (mmWave) frequency range 2 (FR2) bands, by thinning thin-film LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> resonators to sub-50 nm thickness. The high electromechanical coupling (k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and quality factor (Q) of first-order antisymmetric (A1) mode resonators in 128° Y-cut lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) collectively enable the first acoustic filters at mmWave. The key design consideration of electromagnetic (EM) resonances in interdigitated transducers (IDT) is addressed and mitigated. These results indicate that thin-film piezoelectric resonators could be pushed to 5G FR2 bands. Further performance enhancement and frequency scaling calls for better resonator technologies and EM-acoustic filter co-design.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Surface-Mounted Ceramic Filters: Temperature Drift Effect on Coupling Parameters
abstract: This study investigates the impact of temperature on four 3D-printed Alumina bandpass filters. Thermal cycling tests from 23 to 80°C reveal a frequency shift of −766 to −554 kHz/°C, depending on the design. The spatial arrangement of coupling iris structures relative to the heat source affects the inter-resonator coupling factors and the bandwidth drift. The results show bandwidth variations of 42 to 55 kHz/°C and insertion loss changes from 0.004 to 0.006 dB/°C.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Reconfigurable Acoustic Wave Filter with a Large Tuning Range
abstract: This work investigates a new approach to realize bandwidth-reconfigurable acoustic filters. By integrating Phase-Change Material (PCM) switches and composite resonators, the proposed approach provides the flexibility to reconfigure filter bandwidths with a large tuning range while maintaining consistent filter performance.

articleTitle: RF Co-Designed High-Selectivity Bandpass Filter/Attenuator (BPFA) With Tunable Attenuation
abstract: This paper reports on a new type of compact RF co-designed high-selectivity microstrip bandpass filter/attenuator (BPFA) with electronically-reconfigurable attenuation levels in its passband. The reconfigurable attenuation characteristics in the BPFA are obtained by resistively loading two of its capacitively-loaded resonators with PIN diodes. The circuit’s symmetric structure enables analysis through odd and even-mode methods. For proof-of-concept demonstration purposes, an experimental prototype was EM simulated, manufactured, and measured. It demonstrated a 1.2 to 2.4 GHz passband with tunable attenuation levels ranging from 3.47 to 20.24 dB.

articleTitle: 18 GHz Microacoustic ScAlN Lamb Wave Resonators for Ku Band Applications
abstract: This work reports on the designing, manufacturing, and characterization of 18 GHz microacoustic 30% scandium aluminum nitride doped lamb wave Cross-Sectional Lamé Mode Resonators (CLMRs) for K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> band applications, with a specific focus on the next generation of radio frequency filters for 5G and satcom applications.Measured results highlight a 3 dB quality factor (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3dB</inf>) as high as 180, a mechanical quality factor (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) greater than 350, and an electromechanical coupling ($k_t^2$) of 7.5% for 50 Ω matched CLMRs at 18 GHz, while preserving CMOS compatibility, resonant frequency lithographic tunability, and a 3-mask fabrication process. The devices also demonstrated a P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> compression point greater than 12 dBm and a temperature coefficient of frequency of −40 ppm/K.Simulated filter responses based on CLMRs modeling and measured data showcase 3 dB fractional bandwidths (FB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</inf>) greater than 4%, with out-of-band-rejection and selectivity greater than 20 dBc and 15 dBc, respectively, confirming the suitability of the reported technologies for the manufacturing of the next generation of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> band applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Performance in Ladder-Type SAW Filter Using Modified IDT Configurations
abstract: This work investigates the performance of ladder-type Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) filters employing modified Interdigital Transducer (IDT) configurations that can produce resonance with different electromechanical coupling coefficients. By altering the ratio of positive and negative fingers in SAW resonators, discrete coupling coefficient levels can be achieved. Such IDT geometries can impact filter selectivity and asymmetry, providing greater flexibility for different filter specifications.

articleTitle: Tunable Coaxial Resonator Filter based on Posts with Rectangular Bars
abstract: In this paper, a tunable microwave bandpass filter is presented which allows for different center frequency combinations while maintaining a constant bandwidth over a wide frequency range. The special T-shaped form of the coaxial resonator posts allows for adjustment of the center frequency and coupling factor while minimizing the amount of tuning screws. In total, only three tuning elements are used to control the input and inter-resonator coupling as well as the center frequency of the bandpass filter. The filter offers a 57MHz±3MHz bandwidth over a 400MHz frequency range. A demonstrator has been build to verify the concept and exemplary measurements have been taken at 1.73GHz, 1.93GHz and 2.10GHz. The simulations have been compared to the measurements, which validates the 57MHz bandwidth at the 20 dB return loss level for all tuning states.

articleTitle: Multiplexer Equal Ripple Optimization
abstract: Equal ripple optimization of microwave multiplexers is one of the more difficult microwave filter design problems. Defining a strong error function, exact control of passband edge frequencies, numerical efficiency and ease of use are critical issues.

articleTitle: Synthesis of All-Resonator Multiplexers
abstract: This paper presents an iterative method to achieve a strong initial coupling matrix for triggering the subsequent matrix optimization of diplexers/multiplexers with all-resonator topologies. The method is based on the synthesis of a single channel filter in consideration of the estimated loading effect of other channels. The synthesis starts with the characteristic polynomials of each channel filter, obtaining corresponding input admittance, and extracting the equivalent circuit model. Two examples are used to demonstrate the synthesis process and validate the proposed technique. For most topologies, the iterative method converges after less than 20 iterations. The proposed method provides good initial values of the coupling matrix which can substantially reduce the optimization time to seconds, even for complicated topologies.

articleTitle: Aspects of BAW filter harmonics wafer level testing
abstract: Optimal suppression of spurious spikes in the harmonic response of bulk acoustic wave (BAW) filters is becoming a limiting factor to meet the stringent specification requirements in RF modules. The full harmonic (H2) response is typically not characterized during processing the BAW filters, but specification compliance is guaranteed by design on the final module. Outlier screening on final module response is typically done on only a couple of relevant frequency points due to the time intensive nature of the harmonic measurement. In this work we discuss the feasibility of future wafer level screening of BAW filter H2 during processing. Therefore, we discuss a promising probe procedure to emulate the final module response on the wafer. An example is given to demonstrate potential benefits and cost savings of the presented approach by evaluating the performance of different filter designs on a wafer level in a statistical analysis.

articleTitle: Progress on metal Additive Manufactured waveguide filters: from L-band to Q/V-band
abstract: This conference papers presents recent innovations in the domain of waveguide filters fabricated using metal Additive Manufacturing. In particular, two types of filters for space applications are presented: a L-band reconfigurable filter that uses a new type of combline cavity and that achieves x5 mass reduction with respect to classic combline filters at these frequencies; and QV-band output filters with different level of rejection. The article also discusses key design guidelines for the design of such filters,

articleTitle: Advances on Multiplexer Synthesis: The Herringbone Topology
abstract: Current multiplexer synthesis methods have proven to be a reliable tool to start and speed up the design of such a challenging network. However, most of these current methods have focused their attention on star junction multiplexers, which may bring many advantages if compared to other topologies, but may not be convenient in some cases as they do not consider the possible routing and actual connections throughout a multiplexer. This work presents a multiplexer synthesis methodology taking into account the existence of phase shifters or transmission lines along the multiplexer, such as the well-known Herringbone topology.

articleTitle: Robust and Flexible Design for Effective Low-Pass Filters Exploiting a Passband Replica
abstract: In this paper, a design approach for effective low-pass filters (LPF) that use the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>-passband replica of the stepped-impedance prototype response is presented. Traditional LPF design methods often rely on well-established techniques, but they may not always deliver the desired performance or flexibility. By incorporating the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>-passband replica of the stepped-impedance prototype, we introduce a new perspective that opens up new possibilities in filter design. This approach has the potential to overcome some of the limitations associated with existing methods, offering improved filter performance, robustness, and novel design possibilities and flexibility. Additionally, we will showcase its practical application by designing, fabricating, and measuring a 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order gap waveguide LPF that employs the first replica as per the provided guidelines.

articleTitle: Monolithically-Integrated Coaxial Resonator-Based Bandstop Filters Enabled by SLA 3D Printing
abstract: This article reports on a new class of compact, lightweight, monolithically-integrated coaxial cavity resonator-based bandstop filters (BSFs) using stereolithography apparatus (SLA) 3D printing. The BSF concept is based on 3D printed coaxial cavity resonators that are directly coupled by an air-filled coaxial transmission line. Size compactness is achieved by: i) using low-profile sub-wavelength coaxial cavity resonators and by ii) monolithic SLA 3D printing that eliminates the need for assembly screws. For proof of validation purposes, a second-order BSF was designed, manufactured, and measured. Measurement results exhibit a center frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) of 4.5 GHz, stopband rejection of 48 dB, 10 dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 1.7%, and an effective quality factor Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> of 760.

articleTitle: BAW Filter Trends for 5G and Beyond
abstract: Bulk acoustic wave (BAW) filters are a fundamental enabler of 5G wireless communication systems. RF-FEMs feature an ever-increasing number of filter paths that must manage a very crowded electromagnetic spectrum with minimum insertion loss, maximum out-of-band rejection and an unbeatable level of miniaturization. This work presents an overview of the challenges new bands pose for BAW filters along the technological approaches to face them. An example of a hybrid BAW solution for the B41 band with improved rejection is introduced and discussed.

articleTitle: Isolated Filtering System Based on the Emerging AFSIW Technology
abstract: This paper introduces a pioneering passive system in the promising air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) technology. The designed single printed circuit board (PCB) system integrates a filter surrounded by two isolators strategically arranged to mitigate impedance mismatching at its interface and provide high isolation. To do this, the filter and the isolators were designed separately and then assembled together to achieve optimal performance in the satellite Ka frequency band (from 27.5 GHz to 30.2 GHz) with a matching better than 20 dB. A demonstrator was simulated and manufactured for validation. It consists of two isolators and one 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order filter centered at 28.88 GHz with 2.94 GHz bandwidth (BW). The measured demonstrator achieves high rejection with 1.32 dB insertion losses (IL) at the filter center frequency. A frequency shift of 340 MHz and a return loss better than 13 dB were obtained in the experiment. The discrepancy between this first demonstrator and the simulation results is due to fabrication errors, which could be effectively compensated by considering the tolerances of the manufacturing process and implementing some tuning elements in future designs. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, it is the first time a passive system based on the AFSIW technology is reported.

articleTitle: Systematic Synthesis of Synchronous Four Port Filtering Couplers
abstract: This paper presents a synthesis methodology for filtering couplers based on canonical cross-coupled resonators. The synthesis methodology establishes a mapping between the transmission line branch line couplers and the canonical cross-coupled resonator networks. Through this mapping the parameters of a filtering coupler network, which is represented as a coupling matrix, can be obtained. Two synthesis approaches of the parameters of the canonical topology are investigated. A design example employing a rectangular waveguide ten pole filtering coupler is presented as a proof of concept to the usefulness of the design methodology in realizing high power filtering coupler networks.

articleTitle: Metal-Insulator-Metal Capacitor Integration in Bulk Acoustic Wave Filters
abstract: Metal-Insulator-Metal capacitors, MIMCAPs, integrated in bulk acoustic wave technology have proven critical for both performance and size reduction. This paper presents the most efficient technique for an accurate simulation and implementation of these capacitors using full-wave simulators. Some electromagnetic (EM) simulation challenges of MIMCAPs are introduced and the new design approach using low permittivity material is introduced to simulate the MIMCAPs. The measurements demonstrate that the proposed method allows us to implement the MIMCAPs with less than 3 percent inaccuracy during manufacturing.

articleTitle: Novel Compact Tunable Filter Prototype Realized with Vanadium Dioxide
abstract: This paper presents a design, fabrication, and characterization of a reconfigurable filter for use at 25 – 50 GHz. This prototype bandpass filter (BPF) incorporates two poles, and has two bands. In band insertion losses (IL) are simulated as 1.0 and 1.2 dB respectively, and the measured losses are 4.0 dB and 2.5 dB. There is a canonical 12 dB per octave IL roll-off from the pass band. This novel filter uses vanadium dioxide, a phase change material, to vary the length of its coupled transmission lines (TLs). The prototype filter is partially fabricated, and measurements are presented.

articleTitle: Direct Bandpass Synthesis of Wideband Lumped-Elements Filters Using Inductive Couplings
abstract: This paper proposes an alternative way to represent and synthesize any filter network directly in the bandpass domain through the use of the coupling matrix and similarity transformations. For this purpose, a nodal representation is proposed that considers all elements of the filter network individually and independently of the fractional bandwidth. The proposed nodal representation allows the extraction of all lumped-elements directly from the coupling matrix. In this work, the direct bandpass synthesis of a wideband bandpass filter with inductive couplings, classically considered to be a 3rd-order filter in the lowpass prototype domain, is contemplated to validate the proposal.

articleTitle: Synthesizability of Filtenna Arrays with Uniform Quality Factor
abstract: Resonant antennas, such as patches, perfectly fit the paradigm of filtenna arrays in which every element is a lossy resonator. Assuming that its quality factor is mainly dependent upon the chosen technology, a uniform-Q array is thus available. This however imposes strong constraints on the synthesizable reflection functions, with implications on the required elements in order to provide a sufficient gain across the selected passband. A model to describe radiation function and return loss is developed providing the necessary relations with physical parameters, such as gain of the base elements, and tradeoffs when applied to standard transfer functions.

articleTitle: Magnetostatic Wave Notch Filters Frequency Tuned Via a Zero DC Power Magnetic Bias Circuit
abstract: This paper presents a miniature (1.7 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) and zero static power magnetostatic surface wave tunable notch filter with a tuning range from 3.3 GHz – 10.3 GHz. The notch frequency can be directly tuned by transient voltage pulses applied to a magnetic bias circuit, eliminating the need for bulky, power-hungry electromagnets. Aluminium transducers were designed to achieve strong spin wave coupling by direct placement on yttrium iron garnet magnetostatic wave resonators. Low insertion loss was achieved by absorbing the parasitic inductance of the magnetostatic wave resonator transducers into an on-chip LC transmission line. The filter exhibits less than 1.8 dB of insertion and a notch rejection of more than 38 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Tunable Dual-Band Filter to Achieve a Wide Tuning Range Using One Tuning Element
abstract: This paper introduces a new configuration for tunable dual-band filters that can cover a wide tuning range while using just one tuning element. The resonator setup consists of two λ/4 resonators, operating in adjacent frequency bands. These two resonators are connected to conducting rod mounted inside a cavity that is shaped to allow tuning the resonant frequencies of the two resonators as the rod rotates around its axis. The longer resonator covers the lower band of the tuning range, while the shorter one covers the higher band. Importantly, the tunability of these resonators is entirely independent. This means that when one of these resonators is coupled with the input probe, the other one is decoupled, and vice versa. A two-pole tunable filter has been designed with a tuning range from 2 to 3.5 GHz to verify the concept.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable TM-Mode Dielectric Bandpass Filter Using Liquid Metals
abstract: This paper reports on an octave-tunable miniaturized TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf>-mode dielectric bandpass filter based on pneumatically-actuated liquid metals. The resonant frequency is tuned with the movement of the liquid metal which functions as a movable metallic post inside the inner hole of the dielectric resonators. Compared with the conventional screw-based tuning, the proposed technique features faster and more stable tuning process because of the assured excellent electrical contact, continuously for all tuning states. For verification, a second-order TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf>-mode dielectric bandpass filter is designed, fabricated, and tuned using a non-toxic liquid metal alloy commercially known as “Galinstan”. The measured responses exhibit high tuning capabilities with octave tuning ratio of 1:2.22 over a broad window of 1.51 GHz from 1.24 GHz to 2.75 GHz. Further, the presented filter has many desirable merits as the high quality-factor, miniaturized structure, and simple configuration.

articleTitle: Cross-Coupling Simplification in Asymmetric Acoustic-Electromagnetic Filters
abstract: Polynomial function based synthesis methodologies have been extensively studied in the design of acoustic-wave (AW) filters to achieve the filter performance requirements of the application that it is designed for. In order to achieve a desired fractional bandwidth in the presence of an enforced AW resonator electromechanical coupling coefficient, the synthesized filter might incorporate several cross-coupling mechanisms that can be difficult to realize during practical design of the filter. This study proposes a simplification methodology to reduce the required number of cross-coupling mechanisms in the synthesized filters by analyzing the resultant coupling matrices of the design. It has been shown that certain cross-coupling mechanisms can be omitted with minor-to-none out-of-band rejection degradation while keeping the number of finite-frequency transmission zeros the same. As a proof-of-concept, a 14% third-order asymmetrical-response filter is designed and fabricated using electromagnetic resonators and an AW resonator with a $k_t^2$ of 3.5% by reducing the number of the cross-coupling mechanisms from 2 to 1.

articleTitle: Control of the miniaturization degree in BAW CRF filters
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis procedure and circuit transformation for the design of four order CRF BAW filters. Flexibility on the circuit transformation has been included to provide control over the size of the individual resonators and therefore on the size of the overall filter, without much effect on the small signal response of the filter but the losses. For the example presented in this work this process demonstrates a four times reduction on the filter size.This work goes on step further and evaluate the large signal response as well by means of evaluating the nonlinear effects of the final design structure, this is the generation of the second harmonic and IMD. These results reveal the expected increase of nonlinear effects as the size of the filter is reduced.

articleTitle: A 5G n77 Filter Using Shear Bulk Mode Resonator With Crystalline X-cut Lithium Niobate Films
abstract: This paper presents the use of a shear bulk acoustic mode resonator made of a membrane of X-cut lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) for ultra-wide band filter applications. Aluminum interdigitated (IDT) electrodes are deposited on top of the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin film as well as a floating electrode made of aluminum deposited on the backside of the membrane. Through vertical field excitation, shear waves are excited with very good performances. The resonator displays more than 40% of electromechanical coupling at 3.3 GHz and 4.2 GHz. We used simulation and characterization results to synthesize and simulate filters and show the potential of this resonator for wideband filtering applications like the n77 band.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing of Zirconia Dielectric Resonator Filters Produced by Direct Ink Writing of Particles with Bimodal Size Distribution
abstract: Dielectric filters made with additive manufacturing have received attention because even complex geometries can be manufactured. However, the fabrication using, e.g., zirconia is difficult because of the necessity to remove pores with hot isostatic pressing. Here, we present the direct ink writing method of zirconia using more than one particle size to receive dense parts without the need for hot isostatic sintering. To validate this manufacturing process for the production of ceramic resonators for filter applications, the relevant properties, permittivity and loss tangent, are determined. A third order filter made of additively manufactured dielectric TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> mode resonators exhibits an unloaded quality factor of Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 1050 as first demonstrator. It proves the potential of the process used for the cost-effective manufacture of dielectric resonator filters which could also have more complex geometrical structures in future.

articleTitle: Multi-Octave, Reconfigurable Bandpass Filters
abstract: We report on the successful design of a low loss, dynamic center frequency, dynamic bandwidth, highly linear reconfigurable wide-band, multi-octave filer set. This filter assembly is implemented by combining MMICs with RF switches, high Q inductors, and state of the art heterogenous integration. The resulting reconfigurable bandpass filter operates from 0.4 to 4.0 GHz and is the front of a device set that extends to 18 GHz. The filter operates with over 450 filter selections, with contiguous bandpass filters with percent bandwidths from 5% to 50% bandwidth. Insertion loss ranges from 4 to 8 dB based on percent bandwidth and have a predicted IIP3 greater than 43 dBm.

articleTitle: On Modelling of Balanced Filters
abstract: In this paper, a lattice-based model of balanced filters is proposed. The symmetric lattice model is derived directly from the transversal circuit model of coupled-resonators filters through a series of equivalent transformations. Expressions for S-parameters of general symmetric lattice network are derived, as well as equations for S-parameters of balanced bandpass and bandstop filters utilizing the lattice model; the dualism of their transmission and reflection coefficients is demonstrated. Two numerical examples of modelling balanced bandpass and bandstop filters are presented.

articleTitle: Consistent and Cost-Effective PCB-Based D-Band Air-Filled Substrate-Integrated-Waveguide Filters
abstract: Only a limited amount of research has been performed on the implementation of air-filled substrate-integrated-waveguide (AFSIW) systems in multi-layer PCB stacks at subterahertz frequencies. In this paper, we investigate the manufacturing reliability and the measurement repeatability based on several measurements of AFSIW transmission lines and three different filters on three separate PCB panels at D-band frequencies (110 GHz-170 GHz). A promising dual-cavity AFSIW filter with a steep roll-off on both sides of the passband is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured insertion loss is around 3 dB, while the out-of-band suppression is better than 30 dB.

articleTitle: Highly-Compact Dual-Band Bandpass Waveguide Filter Based on Cross-Shaped Frequency-Dependent Coupling
abstract: This work reports the design of an original class of highly-compact dual-band bandpass filter based on dual-mode waveguide resonators inter-coupled through a novel type of frequency-dependent coupling (FDC). The devised FDC consists of a cross-shaped metallic structure placed in the broad wall of a rectangular waveguide. This FDC produces two additional poles and three extra transmission zeros (TZs). Specifically, each pole is surrounded by a pair of TZs, thus generating a dual-band bandpass filtering response. An equivalent lumped-element circuit model of the proposed FDC is provided to facilitate the filter synthesis process. For validation purposes, electromagnetic-(EM)-simulation results for a third-order dual-band bandpass filter design made up of two dual-mode rectangular waveguide resonators inter-coupled with a cross-shaped FDC are presented.

articleTitle: Multi-functional RF Filter with Co-Designed Low Noise Amplifier and RF Switching Capabilities
abstract: This paper presents a co-designed RF bandpass filter and low-noise amplifier (BPF-LNA) with quasi-elliptic transfer function and RF switching capabilities for sub-6 GHz communications. The BPF-LNA concept is based on complex-matched bandpass filtering matching networks (BPF-MN) that directly match the transistor impedances while at the same time achieving bandpass filtering; thus, eliminating the need for RF filters in the RF front-end. Frequency-dependent inter-resonator coupling elements are used in the BPF-MN to enhance the transfer function selectivity by means of transmission zeros (TZs). The concept has been validated at C-band through the design, manufacturing and testing of a BPF-LNA with f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cen</inf> of 4.63 GHz, noise figure (NF) of 2.52 dB and one TZ at the lower side of the passband and a BPF-LNA with two symmetrically-allocated TZs and NF of 2.26 dB. By removing the DC biasing, the BPF-LNAs can be intrinsically switched-off with an isolation > 25 dB within an ultra-broad range.

articleTitle: Management of Stored Energy in Acoustic Wave Ladder Filters to Improve Yield
abstract: The design of acoustic wave ladder is strongly limited by the resonator material properties. That is why transmission zeros, return loss and cut-off frequency are usually controlled independently by adjusting the resonant frequencies of the resonators to meet specifications. However, when a solution has to be mass-produced, the sensitivity of the structure must also be taken into account so that the economical cost is feasible. Consequently, time-consuming post-optimizations are used through very slow statistical analysis to increase yield, leaving aside equiripple solution. This article improves the sensitivity of acoustic wave ladder synthesis so that it can be mass produced efficiently, considering the relationship between stored energy and sensitivity to obtain faster and better results in terms of yield with Generalized Chebyshev functions and even more so with Non-Equiripple functions.

articleTitle: Coupled Resonator Bandpass Filters With Doubly coupled Input/Output
abstract: With the deployment of advanced wireless communication systems that employes massive MIMO antenna arrays, the demands for more practical coupling topologies for bandpass filters with asymmetric filter responses drastically increase. An attractive coupling topology needs to be compact in layout, with fewer/no diagonal couplings, compatible with dual-mode resonator realization and to generate more transmission zeros (TZs). Existing cascaded type of coupling topologies has found difficulties to fulfill the requirements. To this end, a new class of general coupling topologies with doubly coupled I/O ports is proposed in this paper. The new class coupling topologies exhibit two attractive advantages for asymmetric filtering responses: creating more transmission zeros (TZs) and requiring fewer or no diagonal couplings. To synthesize a doubly coupled I/O filter, a simple numerical synthesis method is also introduced. Several examples, including general cases of 8–4 filters with 4 specific practically useful coupling topologies and an 8–5 filter, are given to demonstrate the attractive features of the proposed doubly coupled I/O filters.

articleTitle: Enhancing Numerical Stability in Multiport Network Synthesis with Modified DK Method
abstract: This paper presents a modified Durand-Kerner (DK) method with the aim of improving the suitability for solving the Feldtkeller Equation, specifically in the context of high-order multiplexer synthesis. By refining the initial solution and iteration strategies of the classical DK method, our proposed approach effectively mitigates limitations associated with numerical errors in multiplexer synthesis. The method’s stability is evidenced through comparisons with alternative approaches.

articleTitle: Switch-Based Non-Reciprocal Filter for High-Power Applications
abstract: This paper presents the first switch-based non-reciprocal filter. Compared to varactor-based ones, such designs are more robust against input power, and simpler to bias. Furthermore, the switches, implemented with PIN diodes, consume less power compared to transistor-based non-reciprocal filters. These switches connect extra capacitances to the resonators of the filter, such that switching them ON and OFF creates the necessary time-varying response to achieve non-reciprocity. The concept is designed and implemented on a third-order bandpass filter centered at 1.3 GHz. The measured isolation is 20 dB. The filter is also measured up to 4 W of input power with minimal degradation in performance, while consuming only 15 mW.

articleTitle: Development of Waveguide Filters through Lithography Metal Manufacturing Technology
abstract: This paper reports on a study focused on the implementation of a novel additive manufacturing process, namely the Lithography Metal Manufacturing technology, aimed at the development of waveguide filters. For this technology, an end-to-end manufacturing route based on copper was completely developed from material selection to testing. RF test vehicles operating at 20 GHz and 30 GHz were manufactured to assess dimensional accuracy and electrical conductivity of the printed parts.

articleTitle: Broad Stopband, Wide Passband, Bandstop Filter using the Spurious Bypass Method
abstract: In [1], a method was presented for bypassing spurious passband responses due either to unwanted periodic resonances or of resonances due to parasitics, in a very wideband highpass filter. In that same reference, mention was made for potential application to a bandstop filter, where the bandstop portion is very wide, and the passband is also very wide. In [7] and [8], a lumped-distributed circuit was presented, with a stopband covering 962 MHz to 1210 MHz, with a passband extending to about 6 GHz. In this paper, we have taken the proposed bandstop briefly discussed of [1] and will show that using the proposed bypass method, the same stopband can be achieved, but with a passband extending to 18 GHz. As well, the size of the proposed filter is less than 25% of that of the filter in [7].

articleTitle: Microstrip-to-Microstrip Vertical Transition With Quasi-Elliptic-Type Dual-Band Filtering Response
abstract: A type of two-layer microstrip-to-microstrip (MS-to-MS) vertical transition with quasi-elliptic-type dual-band filtering response is reported. It consists of a MS-to-MS vertical transition on a novel stepped-impedance slotline. To alleviate the radiation losses of the constituent high-impedance slotline sections, two pairs of identical folded low-impedance slotline sections are shunt connected at two ends of the proposed slotline, respectively. By setting the used multiple slotline sections with the specified electrical lengths and impedances, a sharp-rejection third-order dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) response with seven out-of-band transmission zeros (TZs) is attained. The RF operating principle of the conceived vertical transition is discussed by its transmissionline (TL) equivalent circuit. For practical-validation purposes, a proof-of-concept prototype of the devised dual-band MS-to-MS vertical transition is designed, manufactured, and tested. The measured dual-band transition features two sharp-rejection lower and upper passbands with center frequencies of 7.563 and 12.465 GHz, 3-dB fractional bandwidths of 16.86% and 9.7%, minimum in-band power insertion-loss levels of 1.177 dB and 2.104 dB, respectively, and stopband power-attenuation levels above 20 dB from 4.525 to 15.01 GHz (i.e., without considering the passbands).

articleTitle: Staggered Filter Topology for Robust Fabrication of Air-Filled Substrate-Integrated-Waveguide Filters
abstract: In this work, a novel air-filled substrate-integrated waveguide (AFSIW) filter topology is proposed to overcome the challenges of AFSIW printed circuit board (PCB) fabrication by eliminating small protrusions and feature sizes. The topology is further enhanced with a coupling slot to improve the out-of-band rejection by 20 dB. A prototype covering the n257 (26.5 GHz-29.5 GHz) band is synthesized, fabricated and measured to validate the topology, demonstrating its applicability at millimeterwave (mmWave) frequencies with a measured insertion loss of 2.7 dB and out-of-band rejection of over 30 dB.

articleTitle: Exhaustive Synthesis of Microwave Filter Topologies Based on Total Degree Homotopy
abstract: In this paper, total degree homotopy is introduced to exhaustively synthesize microwave filter topologies. This is a reliable and efficient approach that can globally converge to all solutions of the target filter topologies in one run, with no need for repeating the algorithm with different randomized initial guesses. To further adapt to the features of filter topology reconfiguration, the operation that can eliminate the sign symmetry of coupling matrices and reduce computational complexity simultaneously is presented. To validate the proposed theories, one irregular fifth-order topology and one regular sixth-order topology followed by measurement results are synthesized as the examples.

articleTitle: Compact Reconfigurable Matching Network for Antenna Detuning Mitigation in Smart Surfaces
abstract: To address the specific design challenges posed by the Internet of Things (IoT), a compact reconfigurable matching network (RMN) is designed to mitigate detuning of smart-surface-integrated antennas. The RMN is based on a third-order Chebyshev topology, composed of quarter-wavelength stubs, having a well-decoupled varactor at the end of the three shunt stubs. The circuit is designed to mitigate the impedance mismatch between a power amplifier and an antenna being detuned by objects in its reactive near field. The low-loss transmission of the circuit is tuned by controlling the varactor voltages, thereby ideally guaranteeing a low reflection coefficient at all times. Moreover, a systematic investigation of the different loss contributions is performed by means of full-wave simulations that are verified by TRL-calibrated two-port measurements. The RMN is fabricated on a 0.25-mm-thick I-TERA substrate, exploiting printed circuit board (PCB) technology, occupying 20mm×10 mm. Measurement results show that the RMN has a minimum insertion loss of 1.83 dB over the [5.15–5.85] GHz band. Finally, the proposed RMN is validated by correcting a detuned antenna in eleven different representative IoT scenarios, herein optimizing the transducer gain while keeping the input matched at all times.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Input-Reflectionless Filters With Transmission Zeros: First Cauer, Then Foster
abstract: Here describes the application of the ‘first Cauer, then Foster’ concept to the synthesis of input-reflectionless filters with transmission zeros. Synthesis techniques and design equations are fully provided for the readers’ convenience.

articleTitle: Circuit Model Extraction of Coupled-Resonator Filters and Multiplexers Via Direct Use of S-parameter AAA Fitting
abstract: A new method is proposed for coupling matrix extraction for coupled-resonator filters and multiplexers, which directly transforms measured S-parameters to the transversal coupling matrix via the adaptive Antoulas-Anderson (AAA) barycentric rational fitting technique. This method is not dependent on the numerical algorithm that transforms S-parameters to Y-parameters and can be used to overcome the challenge of obfuscated poles in Y-parameter frequency responses.

articleTitle: New Hybrid Filter for Wideband and Better Attenuation Using BAW and IPD Technology
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid High-Pass Filter (HPF) design that combines Bulk Acoustic Wave (BAW) resonator technology with Integrated Passive Device (IPD) technology. While the HPF with IPD resonator exhibits a transmission zero, it is limited by a lack of roll-off responses at the 2469 MHz range. In contrast, our proposed Hybrid Filter, which incorporates both BAW and IPD components, demonstrates superior attenuation performance and boasts an impressive 900 MHz wide-passband. To validate this theory, we conducted fabrication and 3D simulation on the proposed IPD-only filter and the HPF with both IPD and BAW technologies. Notably, the results reveal that the HPF with BAW technology achieves a remarkable 5 dB improvement in attenuation compared to the IPD-only filter.

articleTitle: Design Solutions for Problems in Filters and Structures Using Self-Locking Tuning Screws
abstract: Self-locking tuning screws (SLTS), first introduced by Johanson Manufacturing therefore nicknamed “Johanson Tuning Screw”, provide an easy and fast tuning experience, relative to cumbersome tuning using tuning-bolts and locking nuts. Nevertheless, the internal spring tension embedded in SLTS is due to deep cuts in its body, which weakens the SLTS structure and make it susceptible to fracture. Proper mechanical definitions for thread oversizing and plating thickness should be defined in order to avoid such problems. This paper describes investigation of such problems and detailed design rules which arose from it.

articleTitle: 3D printed Alumina filters for Q band space telecommunication
abstract: This work studies a surface mountable ceramic bandpass filter for Q band application. A 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order Chebyshev filter is designed to have an operating frequency of 40 GHz while optimizing a tradeoff between performances, surface mounting capability and size. Ceramic SLA printing was used to fabricate a specifically designed 3D shape that allows the wire bonding of this filter on a PCB carrier. The filters tested here have been fabricated out of Alumina and attached to a frame in order to facilitate the required technological steps, i.e. full metallization and laser etching of their CPW accesses. The measured results of six filters made within a same batch show a good reproducibility of their measured S-parameters and are in line with the expected performances.

articleTitle: RF Input-Quasi-Reflectionless Dispersive-Delay Structures Based on Complementary-Diplexer Circuits
abstract: A class of RF dispersive-delay structures (DDSs) with input-quasi-reflectionless behavior is reported. It is based on the exploitation of complementary-diplexer circuit networks, in which the out-of-band RF-input-power echoes reflected by the main bandpass-filter-(BPF)-type channel are dissipated by the resistively-terminated auxiliary bandstop-filter-(BSF)-type channel. Specifically, it is shown that the influence of the absorptive auxiliary channel over the in-band transmission-phase response of the main channel can be compensated to obtain the desired transmission-phase profile in the overall RF device. Thus, a multi-functional RF component with co-integrated DDS, BPF, and low-RF-input-reflection capabilities can be designed. Optimization-based synthesis examples at the coupling-routing-diagram level of third-and fifth-order input-quasi-reflectionless BPF-based DDSs, for which the in-band group-delay pattern increases linearly with frequency, are presented. Moreover, for practical-validation purposes, a 2-GHz microstrip prototype is built and measured.

articleTitle: Transitioning from Analytical to Numerical Methods for Synthesizing Microwave Bandpass Filters
abstract: Microwave filters, integral to modern wireless communication systems, have been refined to possess more compact structures and sharper rejection capabilities. The introduction of the theory for exhaustive topology search has led to the development of irregular filter topologies, which couldn’t be synthesized using traditional rotation methods. These novel coupling topologies, such as “trapezoid” and “grid” configurations, are designed to achieve more transmission zeros (TZs) and compact structures. The exhaustive solution search, proposed to identify all possible real-valued solutions for any given topology based on filtering functions, is discussed in detail in this paper. The potency of the mapping between the original coupling matrix and its corresponding folded matrix is demonstrated, with comparisons offered to underline the advantages of the proposed mapping over others. Furthermore, synthesis examples for irregular topologies, including trapezoid and grid topologies, are provided. This method paves the way for the purely analytical synthesis for microwave filters.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Fully Reconfigurable Bandpass Filter with Automated Varactor Biasing
abstract: A miniaturized substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) reconfigurable filter is presented in this paper. The filter is based on quasi-lumped substrate integrated coaxial resonators. Varactors are used as tuning elements to enable a continuous control of all filter parameters. To obtain any targeted response, an automated hardware optimization of the filter is demonstrated based on a single-board computer and a high-voltage varactor driver module. This process enables us to obtain the bias voltages of all varactors for obtaining a particular response. Thus, a twopole filter example, with a compact size of 5.60×5.85 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has been designed, manufactured and measured, showing different reconfiguration scenarios, both in terms of absolute bandwidth and frequency in the n77 and n78 5G channels.

articleTitle: The Resonant Input: Pushing The Boundaries Of Coaxial Comb-Line Evanescent Mode Filters
abstract: This paper extends the state-of-the-art of the coaxial comb-line evanescent mode technology by introducing a unique filter structure capable of reaching performance previously unattainable. A very wide passband, wide stopband, high-power handling capability, as well as a relatively high frequency of operation, are all concurrently accomplished by this new filter. Specifically, the filter showcases an 8–18 GHz passband (covering both X-band and Ku-band) with an upper stopband up to 40 GHz, while guaranteeing a power handling capability of at least 150 W CW. The key idea underlying such an accomplishment is what we call resonant input, which consists of an additional resonance properly generated within the input connector line so as to serve as the first conceptual resonator of the filter. The resonant input makes it possible to maximize the achievable input coupling, which commonly represents the primary aspect limiting the bandwidth of a filter; at the same time, it also significantly alleviates the second typical limitation concerning the amount of inter-resonator coupling within the first pair of resonators. The experimental results of a filter product prove the proposed innovation.

articleTitle: Synthesis of the Acoustic Wave H-Ladder Filter Topology
abstract: The ladder topology is the workhorse in acoustic wave (AW) filter modules because of the high selectivity with low losses that it provides. However, the main limitation is that the achievable bandwidth and the distance of the transmission zeros (TZs) to the passband are limited to the electromechanical coupling coefficient $k_t^2$ of the resonators. Moreover, the strong requirements in terms of area also demand for more compact solutions. For these reasons, a new compact topology is proposed in which there is more flexibility in the allocation of the TZs. This topology has been named H-Ladder and it is based on the conventional ladder, but it uses double shunt resonators at the input and output ports. However, it requires a proper definition of the transfer function to achieve it.

articleTitle: Properties of Triplets with Complex Reflection Zeros
abstract: This manuscript investigates intrinsic properties of triplets, as one of the basic blocks to implement a finite transmission zero. Specifically, some phenomena occurring in common synthesis problems are addressed: extreme external coupling, severe detuning of the resonators, mixed signs for cross-coupling. The objective is to study such occurrences, resorting to algebraic analysis of the problem and to specific analyses when the Reduced Chebychev response is invoked with complex reflection zeros. Relevant properties of the polynomials are described and proven when possible, while approximations are introduced otherwise. Synthesized examples support the validity of the approach.

articleTitle: Monolithic FDM 3-D Printed Waveguide Filters
abstract: In this paper, the design and realization of X-band monolithic 3-D printed waveguide filters is discussed. All proposed filters are manufactured with the low-cost fused deposition modeling (FDM) additive manufacturing technique, due to the wide distribution of this printing technology in laboratories and industry. Two combined waveguide components are proposed: The first component is a combination of a twist and a third order filter while the second one combines a fourth order filter with two frequency dependent couplings, a twist and a corner. All components are manufactured with the FDM printing technique and the results are compared with the simulation. Additionally, the metal plating procedure is shortly addressed.
